question: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series. The resistance of the combination is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**11 Ω.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Three resistors of **2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω **are connected in** series.**
 
• The formula for the total resistance of resistors connected in series is **R_total = R1 + R2 + R3 + ... + Rn.**
 
• Applying this formula, we get the total resistance of the combination as 2 Ω + 3Ω + 6 Ω = **11 ****Ω**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **11Ω.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​When the **same amount of current** passes through each resistor in a set of two or more, the resistors are said to be **connected in series.**

 
 
• The **voltage **across every resistor in these circuits** varies. **
 
 
 
• If the **voltage** is the** same **across all of the resistors, then two or more resistors are said to be **connected in parallel.**
 
 
• When branches in these circuits come together at a common spot, the** current branches out** and recombines.
